0.title: Let the Peoples Praise You, O God
0.overview:
God's plan has always been global. From the promise to Abraham that in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed (Gen 12:3) to John's vision of a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation (Rev 7:9), the Bible tells the story of God gathering worshippers from every people on earth.

Missions is not an optional extra for a few enthusiastic Christians. It is at the heart of God's purpose and the church's calling. Jesus' last command was to make disciples of all nations (Matt 28:19). Every Christian has a part to play: some go, many send, all pray.

The Evangelism study focuses on sharing the faith with those around us. This study widens the view to the whole world. It traces God's heart for the nations through Scripture, looks at the Great Commission and the mission in Acts, considers how Christians can go, send and pray, and ends with the goal: worship from every tribe and tongue.

Five units: (1) God's Heart for the Nations; (2) The Great Commission; (3) The Mission in Acts; (4) Going, Sending and Praying; (5) Every Tribe and Tongue.

1.title: God's Heart for the Nations
1.overview:
From the beginning. God created all humanity in his image and told them to fill the earth (Gen 1:28). After the scattering at Babel, God did not abandon the nations. He called Abraham so that through him all families of the earth would be blessed (Gen 12:3). Israel was chosen not instead of the nations, but for their sake.

A light to the nations. God said to his Servant, It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to bring back the preserved of Israel; I will make you as a light for the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth (Isa 49:6). The Messiah's mission would reach far beyond Israel.

The Psalms sing it. Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples! (Ps 96:3). Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you! (Ps 67:3). Israel's worship anticipated the day when all nations would worship the LORD.

Foreigners in Israel's story. Rahab of Jericho, Ruth the Moabite, Naaman the Syrian, the widow of Zarephath and the Ninevites in Jonah's day: the Old Testament repeatedly shows God's grace reaching beyond Israel.

Jonah. Jonah ran from God's call to preach to Nineveh, Israel's enemy, because he knew God was merciful (Jonah 4:2). When Nineveh repented, God spared it, and Jonah was angry. God's final question to him reveals his heart: And should not I pity Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than 120,000 persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also much cattle? (Jonah 4:11). God cares for the nations, even when his people do not.
1.theology:
Mission begins with God: Mission is first God's work. The Father sent the Son, and the Father and Son sent the Spirit. The church's mission flows from God's own mission (John 20:21).

Israel's calling: Israel was to be a kingdom of priests (Exod 19:6), representing God to the nations. Too often, Israel failed. But God's purpose remained, fulfilled in Christ, the true Israel and light to the nations.

The glory of God: The ultimate goal of missions is the glory of God. Missions exists because worship does not yet fill the earth. For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea (Hab 2:14).
1.examples:
Then: Naaman, commander of the Syrian army, came to Israel seeking healing from leprosy. A captured Israelite servant girl had told his wife about Elisha (2 Kgs 5:2-3). Through her witness, a foreign general came to confess, there is no God in all the earth but in Israel (2 Kgs 5:15).

Now: A church that has always focused on its own neighbourhood begins studying God's heart for the nations. Members start praying for unreached peoples and supporting a missionary family. Their vision of God grows, and so does their love for the world.

A simple test: Do you share God's heart for the nations, or does your concern stop at your own community?

verseByVerse.quote: Now the LORD said to Abram, "Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you. And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and him who dishonors you I will curse, and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God calls Abram and promises to bless him and make him a great nation. But the promise does not end with Abram: in him all the families of the earth will be blessed. God's plan of salvation was global from its first announcement.

verseByVerse.quote: May God be gracious to us and bless us and make his face to shine upon us, Selah that your way may be known on earth, your saving power among all nations. Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you! Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations upon earth. Selah Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you! The earth has yielded its increase; God, our God, shall bless us. God shall bless us; let all the ends of the earth fear him! (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The psalmist prays for God's blessing on Israel, so that God's way may be known on earth and his salvation among all nations. Then he calls all the peoples to praise God. Israel's blessing was meant to overflow to the world.

verseByVerse.quote: And now the LORD says, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him; and that Israel might be gathered to him— for I am honored in the eyes of the LORD, and my God has become my strength— he says: "It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to bring back the preserved of Israel; I will make you as a light for the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The Servant's mission is not only to restore Israel, but to be a light for the nations, bringing God's salvation to the end of the earth. Paul and Barnabas later quoted this verse to explain their mission to the Gentiles (Acts 13:47).

verseByVerse.quote: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry. And he prayed to the LORD and said, "O LORD, is not this what I said when I was yet in my country? That is why I made haste to flee to Tarshish; for I knew that you are a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and relenting from disaster. Therefore now, O LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live." And the LORD said, "Do you do well to be angry?" Jonah went out of the city and sat to the east of the city and made a booth for himself there. He sat under it in the shade, till he should see what would become of the city. Now the LORD God appointed a plant and made it come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to save him from his discomfort. So Jonah was exceedingly glad because of the plant. But when dawn came up the next day, God appointed a worm that attacked the plant, so that it withered. When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on the head of Jonah so that he was faint. And he asked that he might die and said, "It is better for me to die than to live." But God said to Jonah, "Do you do well to be angry for the plant?" And he said, "Yes, I do well to be angry, angry enough to die." And the LORD said, "You pity the plant, for which you did not labor, nor did you make it grow, which came into being in a night and perished in a night. And should not I pity Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than 120,000 persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also much cattle?" (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jonah was angry that God spared Nineveh. God provided a plant to shade him, then removed it, and Jonah was angry again. God asked whether Jonah should pity a plant, while God should not pity a great city full of people. The book ends with God's question, challenging every believer's heart.

1.reflection:
How does Genesis 12:3 show that God's plan was global from the start?

What does Jonah teach us about God's heart and ours?

Which Old Testament stories show God's grace to foreigners?

How could your church grow in concern for the nations?

2.title: The Great Commission
2.overview:
Before he ascended, Jesus gave his disciples their marching orders.

All authority. All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me (Matt 28:18). The commission rests on Christ's universal authority. Because he is Lord of all, all nations must hear of him.

Make disciples. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you (Matt 28:19-20). The goal is not merely converts but disciples: people who follow Christ, are baptised into his church and are taught to obey him.

All nations. The word "nations" refers to peoples, ethnic and language groups, not just countries. Christ's commission reaches every people group on earth.

I am with you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age (Matt 28:20). The commission comes with a promise. Missionaries and witnesses do not go alone.

Repentance and forgiveness. Luke records it differently: that repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem (Luke 24:47). The message is Christ crucified and risen, and the call is to repent and believe.

Sent as Jesus was sent. In John, Jesus says, As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you (John 20:21). The church continues Jesus' mission in the world, empowered by the Spirit.
2.theology:
For every generation: The Great Commission was not only for the apostles. Jesus promised to be with his people to the end of the age, showing that the commission continues until he returns.

Sovereignty and mission: Reformed Christians believe God has chosen his people. Far from discouraging missions, this gives confidence. God has people in every nation whom he will call (Acts 18:10). Our preaching is the means by which he gathers them.

The church's central task: Making disciples of all nations is not one activity among many for the church. It is central to its reason for existing between Christ's ascension and return.
2.examples:
Then: The disciples who received the Great Commission were ordinary men, mostly fishermen, who had recently fled when Jesus was arrested. Within a generation, the gospel had reached across the Roman world. Christ's authority and presence made the difference.

Now: A young couple, both professionals, sense God calling them to serve among an unreached people. Their church tests the call, trains them and commits to send and support them. They go, trusting Christ's promise to be with them.

A simple test: How are you personally involved in the Great Commission?

verseByVerse.quote: Now the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain to which Jesus had directed them. And when they saw him they worshiped him, but some doubted. And Jesus came and said to them, "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The eleven met the risen Jesus on a mountain. Some worshipped; some doubted. Jesus claimed all authority and sent them to make disciples of all nations, baptising and teaching. He promised his presence to the end. The commission is given to imperfect followers, backed by a perfect Lord.

verseByVerse.quote: Then he said to them, "These are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that everything written about me in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms must be fulfilled." Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures, and said to them, "Thus it is written, that the Christ should suffer and on the third day rise from the dead, and that repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. You are witnesses of these things. And behold, I am sending the promise of my Father upon you. But stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus opened his disciples' minds to understand the Scriptures. The Christ would suffer and rise, and repentance and forgiveness would be preached to all nations. The disciples were witnesses, and they would receive power from on high. Mission is rooted in Scripture and empowered by the Spirit.

verseByVerse.quote: On the evening of that day, the first day of the week, the doors being locked where the disciples were for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, "Peace be with you." When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. Then the disciples were glad when they saw the Lord. Jesus said to them again, "Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, even so I am sending you." And when he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, "Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you withhold forgiveness from any, it is withheld." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The risen Jesus appeared to fearful disciples behind locked doors. He gave them peace, showed them his wounds, and sent them as the Father had sent him. He breathed on them, saying, Receive the Holy Spirit. Mission flows from Christ's peace and the Spirit's power.

verseByVerse.quote: And the Lord said to Paul one night in a vision, "Do not be afraid, but go on speaking and do not be silent, for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many in this city who are my people." And he stayed a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: In Corinth, the Lord told Paul in a vision not to be afraid but to keep speaking, for I have many in this city who are my people. God's sovereign election gave Paul confidence to stay and preach. He remained a year and a half.

2.reflection:
What is the difference between making converts and making disciples?

Why does the Great Commission begin with Christ's authority and end with his presence?

How does God's sovereignty encourage missions?

How could you be more involved in the Great Commission?

3.title: The Mission in Acts
3.overview:
The book of Acts shows the Great Commission being carried out.

Widening circles. Jesus said his disciples would be witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth (Acts 1:8). Acts follows this pattern: Jerusalem (chapters 1-7), Judea and Samaria (chapters 8-12), and the wider world (chapters 13-28), ending with Paul preaching in Rome.

Breaking barriers. The gospel crossed every barrier. Samaritans, despised by Jews, received the word (Acts 8). An Ethiopian official was baptised (Acts 8). Peter was sent to the Roman centurion Cornelius, and the Spirit fell on Gentiles (Acts 10). The church learned that God shows no partiality.

Through persecution. After Stephen's death, persecution scattered believers, and those who were scattered went about preaching the word (Acts 8:4). God used opposition to spread the gospel.

A sending church. In Antioch, the church was worshipping and fasting when the Holy Spirit said, Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them (Acts 13:2). After fasting and prayer, they laid hands on them and sent them off. The first missionary journey began with a local church sending its best leaders.

Planting churches. Paul's strategy was to preach in cities, plant churches, appoint elders and move on, later returning or writing to strengthen them (Acts 14:21-23). Missions is not only evangelism but church planting.

Guided by God. Paul's plans were sometimes blocked by the Spirit, and then a vision led him to Macedonia: Come over to Macedonia and help us (Acts 16:9). God directs his mission.
3.theology:
The Spirit drives mission: In Acts, the Holy Spirit empowers, directs and confirms the mission at every step. Mission depends on him, not on human strategy alone.

The local church sends: Missions in Acts is rooted in local churches. Churches send, support and receive reports from missionaries (Acts 14:26-27).

Unfinished: Acts ends with Paul preaching with all boldness and without hindrance (Acts 28:31). The story is open-ended. The mission continues through the church today.
3.examples:
Then: In Philippi, the first converts in Europe were a businesswoman named Lydia, a slave girl freed from an evil spirit, and a jailer and his household (Acts 16). The gospel reached the wealthy, the enslaved and the ordinary. The church in Philippi became Paul's faithful partner in mission.

Now: A small church realises it has never sent anyone into missions. They begin praying, as Antioch did. Two years later, a young member senses a call to Bible translation. The church commissions her, laying hands on her, and supports her for years.

A simple test: Has your church ever sent someone into missions? How could it become a sending church?

verseByVerse.quote: So when they had come together, they asked him, "Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?" He said to them, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by his own authority. But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The disciples asked about the timing of the kingdom. Jesus redirected them to their task: be witnesses, empowered by the Spirit, from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth. The rest of Acts unfolds this verse.

verseByVerse.quote: Now there were in the church at Antioch prophets and teachers, Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen a lifelong friend of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul. While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." Then after fasting and praying they laid their hands on them and sent them off. So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The church at Antioch had a diverse leadership. As they worshipped and fasted, the Spirit called Barnabas and Saul. The church fasted, prayed, laid hands on them and sent them off. The missionaries were sent out by the Holy Spirit and by the church together.

verseByVerse.quote: And they went through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia. And when they had come up to Mysia, they attempted to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them. So, passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas. And a vision appeared to Paul in the night: a man of Macedonia was standing there, urging him and saying, "Come over to Macedonia and help us." And when Paul had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go on into Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul and his companions were forbidden by the Spirit to preach in Asia and prevented from entering Bithynia. Then Paul saw a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading for help. They concluded that God had called them. God guides mission through closed doors as well as open ones.

verseByVerse.quote: For "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved." How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, "How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!" But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed what he has heard from us?" So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Everyone who calls on the Lord will be saved. But how can they call on one they have not believed, believe in one they have not heard of, or hear without someone preaching? And how can they preach unless they are sent? Missions is necessary because faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.

3.reflection:
How does Acts 1:8 provide the outline for the book of Acts?

What barriers did the gospel cross in Acts? What barriers must it cross today?

What can your church learn from the church in Antioch?

Why is Romans 10:14-15 a powerful argument for missions?

4.title: Going, Sending and Praying
4.overview:
Every Christian has a role in missions. Some go, many send, and all pray.

Going. God calls some believers to leave home and take the gospel to other peoples. Paul's ambition was to preach the gospel, not where Christ has already been named (Rom 15:20). Missionaries may be church planters, Bible translators, teachers, medical workers or professionals who live and work among unreached people. Going is costly, but Jesus promised that no one who leaves home for his sake will lose out (Mark 10:29-30).

Sending. Those who go need those who send. John commended a church for supporting travelling missionaries: You will do well to send them on their journey in a manner worthy of God... Therefore we ought to support people like these, that we may be fellow workers for the truth (3 John 6, 8). Senders give money, practical help, encouragement and friendship. The Philippian church supported Paul repeatedly, and he called them partners in the gospel (Phil 1:5; 4:15-16).

Praying. Jesus said, The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest (Matt 9:37-38). Paul asked churches to pray for open doors and boldness (Col 4:3-4). Prayer is not the least we can do; it is essential.

Welcoming. Many people from other nations now live nearby: students, migrants, refugees. Christians can reach the nations without leaving home, through hospitality and friendship.

Unreached peoples. Many people groups still have little or no access to the gospel. Missions should give special priority to those who have never heard, as Paul did.
4.theology:
The call to go: How does someone know whether God is calling them to go? Usually through a growing desire, godly character, relevant gifts, the confirmation of the local church and open doors. The church should test and affirm such callings (Acts 13:2-3).

Generosity: Supporting missions is an act of worship. Paul called the Philippians' gift a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God (Phil 4:18).

Faithfulness and fruit: Some missionaries see much fruit; others labour for years with little visible result. Faithfulness, not success, is what God requires (1 Cor 4:2).
4.examples:
Then: The church at Philippi sent gifts to Paul more than once, even when they were poor. Paul promised them, And my God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus (Phil 4:19). Those who give to missions are cared for by God.

Now: An elderly widow cannot go abroad, but she prays every day for the missionaries her church supports, writes them letters and gives sacrificially from her pension. When one missionary returns home, he visits her first and tells her that her prayers carried him through his hardest years.

A simple test: Are you a goer, a sender or a pray-er? Could you be more than one?

verseByVerse.quote: For I will not venture to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience—by word and deed, by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God—so that from Jerusalem and all the way around to Illyricum I have fulfilled the ministry of the gospel of Christ; and thus I make it my ambition to preach the gospel, not where Christ has already been named, lest I build on someone else's foundation, but as it is written, "Those who have never been told of him will see, and those who have never heard will understand." This is the reason why I have so often been hindered from coming to you. But now, since I no longer have any room for work in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to come to you, I hope to see you in passing as I go to Spain, and to be helped on my journey there by you, once I have enjoyed your company for a while. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul describes his ambition to preach where Christ had not been named, so that those who had not heard would understand. He planned to go to Spain, hoping the church in Rome would help him on his journey. Paul combined pioneering zeal with dependence on supporting churches.

verseByVerse.quote: Beloved, it is a faithful thing you do in all your efforts for these brothers, strangers as they are, who testified to your love before the church. You will do well to send them on their journey in a manner worthy of God. For they have gone out for the sake of the name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles. Therefore we ought to support people like these, that we may be fellow workers for the truth. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John praises Gaius for supporting travelling missionaries, even strangers. They had gone out for the sake of the name, accepting nothing from unbelievers. Therefore believers should support them, becoming fellow workers for the truth. Senders share in the work.

verseByVerse.quote: And Jesus went throughout all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every affliction. When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd. Then he said to his disciples, "The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus saw the crowds, harassed and helpless like sheep without a shepherd, and had compassion. He told his disciples to pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out labourers. Compassion leads to prayer, and prayer leads to sending.

verseByVerse.quote: Yet it was kind of you to share my trouble. And you Philippians yourselves know that in the beginning of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church entered into partnership with me in giving and receiving, except you only. Even in Thessalonica you sent me help for my needs once and again. Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that increases to your credit. I have received full payment, and more. I am well supplied, having received from Epaphroditus the gifts you sent, a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God. And my God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul thanks the Philippians for sharing in his troubles and supporting him repeatedly. Their gift was a fragrant offering to God. Paul assures them that God will supply all their needs. Giving to missions is an investment in eternity.

4.reflection:
Are you a goer, a sender or a pray-er? How might God be calling you?

How could you support a missionary more practically?

Pray Matthew 9:38 for a specific missionary or people group this week.

How could you reach people from other nations who live near you?

5.title: Every Tribe and Tongue
5.overview:
The goal. John saw the end of the story: After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and crying out with a loud voice, "Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!" (Rev 7:9-10). Missions will succeed. Every people will be represented before the throne.

Ransomed by the Lamb. The new song of heaven celebrates the Lamb: for you were slain, and by your blood you ransomed people for God from every tribe and language and people and nation (Rev 5:9). Christ's death is the price of a worldwide people.

Before the end. Jesus said, And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come (Matt 24:14). History is moving toward this goal.

Only one way. Missions is urgent because salvation is found only in Christ. And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). Sincere followers of other religions are not saved by their sincerity. They need to hear of Christ.

Confidence. Because God has promised a people from every nation, missions cannot fail. Missionaries may suffer and die, as many have. But the gospel will reach the ends of the earth. The Lamb will have his reward.

Joy. The goal of missions is the joy of the nations in God. Let the nations be glad and sing for joy (Ps 67:4). Missions brings the greatest good to people: knowing and enjoying God forever.
5.theology:
The exclusivity of Christ: Some suggest that all religions lead to God, or that people can be saved without hearing of Christ. Scripture says otherwise (John 14:6; Acts 4:12; Rom 10:14). This is not narrowness but the reason for urgency. The Apologetics study addresses this further.

Diversity in unity: The multitude in Revelation is not uniform. It is from every nation, tribe and language. God delights in the diversity of human cultures, redeemed and united in Christ.

Worship as the goal: Missions is a means; worship is the end. When all the redeemed stand before the throne, missions will be over, but worship will last forever.
5.examples:
Then: At Pentecost, people from every nation under heaven (Acts 2:5) heard the gospel in their own languages. It was a foretaste of Revelation 7:9, the beginning of the reversal of Babel.

Now: A Bible translator works for decades to translate the New Testament into a language spoken by a small people group. When the first copies arrive, the believers there weep and sing as they read God's word in their heart language for the first time. Another tribe has been added to the song.

A simple test: Does the vision of Revelation 7:9 move you? How could it shape your prayers and giving?

verseByVerse.quote: After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and crying out with a loud voice, "Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!" And all the angels were standing around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God, saying, "Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might be to our God forever and ever! Amen." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: John sees a multitude beyond counting from every nation, tribe, people and language, worshipping God and the Lamb. Angels and elders fall on their faces in worship. This is the goal of all missions: a worldwide people praising God forever.

verseByVerse.quote: And they sang a new song, saying, "Worthy are you to take the scroll and to open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you ransomed people for God from every tribe and language and people and nation, and you have made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they shall reign on the earth." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The new song celebrates the Lamb who was slain. By his blood he ransomed people for God from every tribe, language, people and nation, and made them a kingdom and priests. The cross is the foundation of missions, and its fruit is a worldwide people.

verseByVerse.quote: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders, if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, by what means this man has been healed, let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—by him this man is standing before you well. This Jesus is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone. And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter, filled with the Spirit, tells the council that the lame man was healed by the name of Jesus, whom they crucified and God raised. Salvation is found in no one else. There is no other name. This truth drives the urgency of missions.

verseByVerse.quote: And because lawlessness will be increased, the love of many will grow cold. But the one who endures to the end will be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus warns that lawlessness will increase and love grow cold, but the one who endures will be saved. And the gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations before the end comes. History is moving toward the completion of the mission.
